headline: Premium growth and buybacks lift earnings; guidance raised
summary_short: Globe Life's Q2 FY2026 diluted EPS rose 20% y/y to $3.65 on 7% total premium growth and a 4.7% reduction in diluted share count; net income climbed 14% to $287.7M. The company raised full-year 2026 net operating EPS guidance to $15.55-$15.95, up $0.10 at the midpoint.
summary_long: Total premium revenue grew 7% y/y (health +16%, led by United American +29%; life +3%), and net investment income rose 4%, lifting total revenue 8% to $1.600B. Insurance underwriting income rose 5% as life underwriting margin gained 6% and health margin gained 1%. Net income rose 14% y/y to $287.7M and diluted EPS rose 20% to $3.65, boosted by a 4.7% drop in diluted shares outstanding following $175M of buybacks (1.1M shares) in the quarter. Shareholders' equity rose to $6.156B; book value per share increased 18% y/y to $78.18 ($100.04 ex-AOCI) as the AOCI drag narrowed versus a year ago. Management raised full-year 2026 net operating income per diluted share guidance to $15.55-$15.95, up $0.10 at the midpoint.

drivers.explanation: Eighth double-digit operating-EPS growth quarter in the last nine; management cited broad-based premium growth across divisions plus continued share repurchases.
Total premium revenue grew 7% y/y; health premium +16% (United American +29%, Family Heritage +9%) outpaced life premium +3%. Net investment income rose 4%.
Insurance underwriting income rose 5% (life margin +6%, health margin +1%) and excess investment income rose 10%, partly offset by higher interest expense and taxes.
EPS growth (+20%) outpaced net income growth (+14%) because weighted diluted shares fell 4.7% y/y after $175M of buybacks (1.1 million shares) this quarter.
Book value per share rose 18% y/y to $78.18 (11% ex-AOCI to $100.04); the AOCI headwind narrowed to $1.72B from $1.98B a year ago.
